original_question: Determine whether there exists an absolute constant c>0 such that for every t>=3, any family F of labelled graphs on [n] whose pairwise intersections all have chromatic number at least t satisfies |F| <= 2^{C(n,2)-c t^2}.
target_in_paper: Section 4, Conjecture 4.4 (the weaker conjecture following Conjecture 4.3 in 'Some problems on intersecting families of graphs').
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right target almost exactly: it asks for an absolute constant c>0, quantifies over t>=3, considers families of labelled graphs on [n], imposes the chromatic-number condition on intersections G∩H, and asks for the quadratic-exponent upper bound |F| <= 2^{binom(n,2)-ct^2}. This matches the paper's Conjecture 4.4 rather than the stronger Conjecture 4.3.
missing_details: The paper quantifies over every n in addition to every t>=3; this should be stated explicitly.
The graphs are simple labelled graphs on the fixed vertex-set [n]={1,2,...,n}, equivalently elements of P(binomial([n],2)); this identification is explicit in Conjecture 4.4.
The intersection G∩H is edgewise intersection of graphs on the same labelled vertex-set; this should be spelled out for stand-alone clarity.
The hypothesis in the paper is 'for all G,H in F', not merely for distinct pairs; in particular each G in F also satisfies chi(G)>=t because G∩G=G.
'Absolute constant' means independent of both n and t; that independence should be explicit.
The question is not asymptotic ('for sufficiently large n'); the conjectured bound is for all n and all t>=3.
To stay paper-faithful, it helps to indicate that this is the weaker quadratic-exponent version of the sharper Conjecture 4.3, whose predicted exponent is binom(t,2).
refined_question: Does there exist an absolute constant c>0 such that, for every n in N and every integer t>=3, whenever F is a family of simple labelled graphs on the vertex-set [n]={1,2,...,n} (equivalently F⊂P(binomial([n],2))) with the property that chi(G∩H)>=t for all G,H in F, where G∩H denotes edgewise intersection, one has |F|<=2^{binom(n,2)-ct^2}?
justification: The draft is targeting the graph-intersection problem in Section 4, not the hypercube material from Section 1. The exact nearest formulation is Conjecture 4.4, which asks for a universal quadratic improvement over the trivial 2^{binom(n,2)} scale under the hypothesis chi(G∩H)>=t for all G,H in F. The surrounding context matters: Section 4 defines the ambient setting of labelled graphs on [n] and graph intersection; Proposition 4.2 gives the currently easy entropy-based bound 2^{binom(n,2)-t+1}; and Conjecture 4.3 states the sharper hoped-for bound 2^{binom(n,2)-binom(t,2)}. Conjecture 4.4 is then presented explicitly as the weaker open conjecture that still remains unresolved.
